messages:

Subject: MSA term questions and proposed redlines

Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal and procurement reviewed the MSA and we have two primary asks that will determine whether we can sign quickly: a shorter auto-renew cadence and a clearer off-ramp for our pilot phase. High-level asks: 1) change auto-renew to 6 months (pilot-level commitment), 2) 60-day notice window for non-renewal, 3) limit or remove broad "termination for convenience" language during the pilot so we can avoid long tail billing if we wind down.

I attached a marked-up MSA with tracked changes (ACME_MSA_redlines_v1.docx). We can be flexible on notice wording if that enables a faster path to signature. Marcus (cc'd) is on procurement and will help prioritize.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a 6-month renew cadence for pilot customers with a pro-rata refund on pre-paid periods if the pilot is cancelled? If you need legal to weigh in, please loop them in and we can aim to close before the end of the month.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Jones
Head of Procurement, Acme Analytics

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear asks and the redline. Quick response: we want to be pragmatic for pilots, and we have levers to make this work but need to align internally on any permanent MSA changes. High-level thoughts: 
- 6-month auto-renew for pilot-sized commitments is reasonable as a one-off for Acme; our standard enterprise Order Form still prefers 12 months.
- 60-day notice is OK (we typically do 30-90 depending on billing cycles).
- Removing TFC entirely is unlikely, but we can negotiate a pilot carve-out: keep a limited TFC that’s capped (e.g., 30 days of fees) or require a shorter notice. We should also define refund/proration mechanics clearly on prepaid credits.

Looping in Laura (sales ops) and Karthik (legal) to confirm acceptable phrasing and get an internal redline out. If legal can prepare a proposed Order Form that implements the pilot carve-out + proration language, we can share a DocuSign link.

Next step: Karthik / Laura — can you review Samantha's attached doc and propose clean language (or an order form amendment) that we can send back to Acme by Monday?

—Ben
Ben Carter

Samantha / Ben —

Thanks for the redline and context. I reviewed ACME_MSA_redlines_v1.docx and have the following recommended approach that balances Acme's need for flexibility and Redwood's commercial protections: 

1) Pilot-specific Order Form Addendum: create a short addendum attached to the Order Form that specifies pilot coverage. Key points: 
   - Term: 6 months initial term for the pilot only; subsequent renewals fall back to the underlying Order Form term unless both parties agree in writing.
   - Auto-renew: add clause — "Pilot Order Form will automatically renew for successive six (6) month periods unless either party provides written notice at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term."
   - Termination for Convenience (TFC): retain a limited TFC for the pilot with a liquidation cap equal to the greater of (i) remaining prepaid amounts for the then-current month or (ii) thirty (30) days of monthly fees; this prevents open-ended liability but preserves Redwood's ability to offboard.
   - Proration/Refunds: if prepaid credits remain after termination, apply pro-rata refund for unused time less any usage-based tokens consumed; specify invoice adjustment process.

2) Billing & Notice Mechanics: define the notice sent to finance (billing@redwood.com) with a 60-day window; order form should include billing cycle alignment language so that refunds/proration are straightforward.

3) Implementation: Laura — can you produce a clean Order Form addendum (Word) that implements the above? I can then convert to an MSA amendment if Acme wants the change to roll into the Master Services Agreement. If Acme insists on removing TFC entirely, we will need exec approval; that is not our standard.

Samantha — if that approach sounds acceptable I will draft the addendum and extract the minimal MSA edits to keep the redline surface area small. If you prefer we can present this as a one-off Order Form concession that does not alter the Master Services Agreement.

Karthik Iyer
General Counsel (acting), Redwood Inference
